name: Goodnotes
description: Goodnotes is a cross-platform digital notebook for handwriting, typed notes, whiteboards, PDF annotation, study sets and collaborative documents. People use it to capture ideas, organize learning materials, mark up files and work together across Apple devices, Android, Windows and the web.
agentUseSummary: Goodnotes cannot be connected directly to Relay agents because it publishes no supported account API, delegated OAuth contract, API-key contract, local automation interface or remote MCP service. Its subscription-only Email to Goodnotes feature accepts bounded PDF attachments at a user-generated address, but that is an inbound import destination requiring separate trusted email-sender authority rather than a Goodnotes account connection.

blocked.label: Connect a Goodnotes account
blocked.description: Goodnotes does not publish a supported OAuth, API-key, developer-console or remote MCP connection contract for public third-party applications.

blocked.label: Use Goodnotes account data
blocked.description: Goodnotes does not document supported endpoints, schemas, permissions or rate limits for reading or changing a customer's library through an account API.

blocked.label: Automate the Goodnotes app or private service
blocked.description: Relay will not automate Goodnotes' UI, scrape shared or private pages, reverse engineer cloud traffic, inspect app containers, or call non-public interfaces.

blocked.label: Treat inbound email as account access
blocked.description: A generated @goodnotes.email address is a subscription-only PDF import destination, not authentication, library read authority, delivery confirmation or permission to expose that address to agents.

blocked.label: Proxy through a backup provider
blocked.description: Goodnotes Auto Backup is a one-way export copy; editing its Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or WebDAV destination does not change the Goodnotes library.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No direct agent actions can be enabled without a supported Goodnotes account API, local automation contract or remote MCP service.

runtimeSupport.description: No documented public Goodnotes account API, supported local automation interface or remote MCP service is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No documented public Goodnotes account API, supported local automation interface or remote MCP service is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Goodnotes' official material documents interactive apps, link sharing, file import/export, one-way backup and a subscription-only inbound PDF email address, but no supported direct account API, delegated OAuth contract, API-key contract, local automation interface, developer console or remote MCP service. Its terms prohibit automated service access, scraping, non-public interfaces and reverse engineering.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Goodnotes credentials or show Connect. Reconsider a direct connector only if Goodnotes publishes a supported distributable account API, delegated OAuth contract, local automation interface or remote MCP service; treat Email to Goodnotes separately as an approved email-send workflow only after Relay has explicit bounded attachment composition across an independently authorized email connection.

evidence.supports: Goodnotes documents interactive import from the app, external apps, drag and drop and connected storage, with platform-specific file and size limits rather than a programmatic library API.
Goodnotes documents a subscription-only generated email destination that trusted senders may use for PDF attachments up to 25 MB; it supports import only and requires the app to fetch new documents.
Goodnotes states that Auto Backup to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or WebDAV is one-way and that cloud-storage changes do not affect the Goodnotes library.
Goodnotes documents interactive link sharing and browser viewing or signed-in editing, including the public-link access model and owner-controlled revocation.

Goodnotes' terms restrict access to publicly supported interfaces and prohibit automated service access, scraping, non-public areas and reverse engineering, so Relay must not substitute private app or web automation for a missing integration contract.
